Prior to the issuance of any permit or approval for 3 a wind energy conversion facility, the applicant shall submit 4 to the local authority a microplastic and fiberglass emission 5 mitigation plan. The plan shall be prepared by a qualified 6 environmental scientist or professional engineer licensed in 7 the state of Iowa and shall include all of the following: 8 (1) An assessment of the composition of all turbine blade 9 materials, including fiberglass, epoxy resin, polyurethane 10 coatings, and any materials containing bisphenol A or other 11 substances listed on the United States environmental protection 12 agency’s priority pollutant list. 13 (2) An estimate of the annual rate of leading edge erosion 14 for each turbine model proposed, expressed in grams per year 15 per blade, based on peer-reviewed scientific literature or 16 manufacturer data applicable to the wind and precipitation 17 conditions at the proposed site. 18 (3) An analysis of the likely dispersion pattern of 19 microplastic and fiberglass particles from blade erosion, 20 including modeling of wind-driven particle transport, with 21 specific reference to all agricultural land, watercourses, 22 drainage ditches, wetlands, and potable water sources within 23 one mile of any proposed turbine location. 24 (4) A description of the blade coating and leading edge 25 protection systems to be employed, including the manufacturer’s 26 specifications for erosion resistance and estimated effective 27 lifespan of such systems. 28 (5) A schedule for inspection and maintenance of blade 29 coatings and leading edge protection systems, including the 30 criteria that will trigger recoating or blade replacement. 31 (6) A remediation plan describing the measures the 32 applicant will take to identify and remove fiberglass or 33 microplastic contamination of soil, water, or agricultural 34 products on nonparticipating property should such contamination 35 -1- HF 2580.3226 (1) 91 sb/js 1/ 2 #1. occur, whether from gradual erosion or catastrophic blade 1 failure. 2 b. The local authority shall not approve the application 3 unless the local authority finds that the microplastic and 4 fiberglass emission mitigation plan, submitted pursuant to 5 paragraph “a” , adequately addresses the risk of microplastic 6 and fiberglass contamination to agricultural land, water 7 resources, and human health within the affected area. 8 c. The applicant shall file an updated microplastic and 9 fiberglass emission mitigation plan with the local authority 10 no less frequently than every five years following initial 11 commercial operation, or within sixty days following any 12 catastrophic blade failure event, whichever is sooner. 13 d. The microplastic and fiberglass emission mitigation plan, 14 submitted pursuant to paragraph “a” , and all updates thereto 15 shall be public records available for inspection at the office 16 of the county recorder. 17 e. This subsection shall not apply to a renewable electric 18 power generation facility that does not include a wind energy 19 conversion facility. > 20 2.
